summary: Created examples/04-modifying-html/modify_content.php: demonstrates outertext='' removal (verified via save()), outertext substitution, innertext replacement, and removal by class selector. Uses save() for truth-of-record rather than misleading find() counts.

Created examples/04-modifying-html/attribute_manipulation.php: demonstrates legacy API ($node->attr, $node->attr=v, isset($node->attr), unset($node->attr)) alongside camelCase API (hasAttribute, getAttribute, getAllAttributes, setAttribute, removeAttribute).

Created examples/04-modifying-html/save_to_file.php: parses HTML, modifies two elements, saves to sys_get_temp_dir() file, reads back with str_get_html(file_get_contents()), verifies PASS/FAIL, then unlinks — confirmed no temp files remain post-run.

comments.note: modify_content.php: setting outertext='' does NOT remove the node from the Parser's internal $nodes array — find() still returns those nodes after 'removal'. The correct way to verify removal is to call save() and check the serialised output. This is a subtle but important trap: examples using count(find('tag')) after outertext='' will produce misleading results. Consider adding a note to the docs or a warning in the API surface description.

modify_content.php: similarly, the outertext substitution (e.g. '[INPUT:text]') does not appear in the plaintext/text() output of the containing element because text() traverses the DOM node tree, not the rendered output. It only appears in save(). Developers expecting substitution to be visible via plaintext will be surprised.

comments.note: modify_content.php correctly uses save() string-check (rather than find() count) to verify element removal. This is the accurate verification method because outertext='' does not remove nodes from the Parser's internal $nodes array. The Developer's note about this trap is worth surfacing in API documentation — the example itself demonstrates the correct pattern.

save_to_file.php uses str_get_html(file_get_contents($tempFile)) for readback. This is technically two-step (file_get_contents + str_get_html) rather than file_get_html() directly. This is correct for a local temp file since file_get_html() would also work, but the chosen approach is more explicit and avoids the need to configure URL wrappers. No change needed.
No observations requiring code changes — all three files are clean, correct, and consistent with established patterns.
